title: I Tracked 26 CS2 Cases for 8 Months. None Went Up.

beats: I tracked twenty-six CS2 cases, every single day, for almost eight months.
Not one of them went up.
And these are the cases Valve stopped dropping.
Around the turn of the year, the rare drop pool went quiet, and more than thirty old cases lost their main source of new supply.
Supply freezes, scarcity kicks in, prices climb. That's the theory.
It didn't happen. And at the end, I'll show you the one number that would change my mind.
Here's how I measured it. One Steam Market price per case, per day, from mid-March until this week.
Cases that are up? Zero.
The typical case is down twenty-eight percent.
Here's an index of all twenty-six. One hundred is mid-March.
At first, the scarcity story looked right. By early May, the index had reached one hundred and ten.
Then it rolled over. Late June brought the first sharp leg down.
The summer was a slow bleed, until early October delivered the worst seven days in this data, down ten percent.
Today it's sitting around seventy-two, thirty-five percent below the May high.
The damage isn't even.
Snakebite and Clutch have both more than halved. Snakebite went from seventy-six euro cents to thirty-five.
The best performer was the Revolver Case, and it still lost eleven percent.
Spectrum and the Chroma cases held up better too, but nothing here is a winner. They just lost less.
Split a hundred euros evenly across these cases in March, and today you'd be holding about seventy-one, before Steam takes its cut.
So why did frozen supply fail? Because supply is only half the equation.
Look at sales. In March, the average case sold about five thousand two hundred units a day. In October, about two thousand nine hundred. That's forty-five percent fewer.
Players are leaving too. October averaged about seven hundred and ninety-seven thousand concurrent players, sixteen percent below a year earlier.
And cases have more competition. Since October twenty twenty-five, five Covert skins can be traded up for a knife or gloves, and Valve's newest releases are Terminals, not classic cases.
Even the cases still dropping fell. Kilowatt has halved since July.
Here's my read. Scarcity can set up a price move, but it can't create demand.
A frozen supply doesn't matter much when the buyers are leaving.
So the number that would change my mind is daily sales. If that stops falling, the story changes.
Which of these would you hold? Tell me in the comments. This isn't financial advice, and the sources are in the description.
